0.fast: C1 planning → mini-RAG orientation → your scope and diagnostic. Spend hours defining a testable first slice, not choosing a framework.
diagnostic: Backend transfer
Explain validation, auth, persistence and one integration test from CRM.
Python/SQL baseline
Write a JSON transformation and a small join without generated code.
Product reasoning
Name a user, their question, a failure and observable success.
pitfalls: Planning everything
Freeze three non-goals and build the first endpoint next.
Vague AI success
Turn “helpful answer” into groundedness, citation and abstention criteria.
Copying a tutorial product
Use your own reflection/journal user stories and corpus.
questions: What makes the first release small?
One user flow, a small corpus, explicit non-goals and observable acceptance criteria.
What counts as prior skill evidence?
A specific route, test, schema or commit you can explain and modify.
Why draft evaluation questions now?
They expose ambiguous scope and establish a baseline before optimization.

1.fast: F2/F4 selective reading → mini-RAG lessons 5–6 or CS50 testing → a fake-provider API. Add pytest from the first endpoint.
diagnostic: Python transfer
Use functions, OOP, exceptions, modules and virtual environments without a beginner walkthrough.
HTTP transfer
Explain status codes, validation and middleware from Express.
Testing transfer
Write one success and one failure assertion independently.
pitfalls: Annotations treated as validation
Show a plain typed function accepting a bad value and a Pydantic model rejecting it.
One global mutable client/session
Initialize shared clients in lifespan; use request/task-specific state.
Tests call a paid model
Override the provider and make tests deterministic.
questions: Why Depends rather than manual construction in every route?
It provides a declared lifecycle and an override seam while keeping application logic testable.
Does async make CPU work faster?
No; it enables cooperative I/O concurrency. CPU work needs a different execution boundary.
What must cleanup prove?
Resources close on both success and exceptions; tests verify the teardown.

2.fast: Selected Arabic regression/classification or visual math → scikit-learn split/pipeline lab. Keep the scope to foundations that explain AI-system decisions.
diagnostic: Math baseline
Manipulate arrays and explain a mean, probability and function slope.
Python prerequisite
Write functions and load a small tabular dataset.
Application link
Explain why retrieval similarity and predictive confidence are different.
pitfalls: Leakage during preprocessing
Fit transforms only on training data and prove it in a pipeline.
Accuracy on an imbalanced set
Compare to a trivial baseline and inspect precision/recall.
Turning this into a long DS track
Stop after one correct baseline and a short explanation of uncertainty.
questions: What is data leakage?
Training or selection uses information unavailable at prediction time, including test-set preprocessing.
Why normalize vectors?
It changes similarity geometry; cosine compares direction after accounting for magnitude.
Is cosine 0.8 an 80% probability?
No. It is a geometric score, not a calibrated event probability.

3.fast: G1 + C2 conceptual sections → visual attention/backpropagation → a tiny CPU PyTorch lab and one inference endpoint. Train no large model here.
diagnostic: L02 readiness
Explain a loss, gradient, train/test split and vector shape.
Python readiness
Use a small tensor/array and inspect dimensions.
System boundary
Separate a web server process from a model-serving process.
pitfalls: Skipping shapes
Print shape/dtype/device at each step and assert expected dimensions.
Assuming sampling is fully deterministic
Record model/version/config and repeat outputs; temperature zero is not a universal reproducibility guarantee.
Training before integration
Use a CPU toy model for understanding; integrate an existing model for the app.
questions: What does backpropagation compute?
Derivatives of a loss with respect to parameters using the chain rule.
Why do token counts differ in Arabic and English?
The tokenizer vocabulary and segmentation differ; measure the actual model tokenizer.
What is post-training versus inference?
Post-training updates parameters or preferences; inference uses the selected parameters to produce outputs.

4.fast: G2 code section + G3 → one provider adapter → validated output → a fixed prompt comparison. Read C5 for failure analysis after the first call.
diagnostic: L01 readiness
A fake provider can be replaced through a tested dependency.
Model readiness
Explain tokens, sampling and context limits.
Contract readiness
Specify expected response fields and provider error behavior.
pitfalls: Prompt only works for the demo
Use fixed ordinary, ambiguous and adversarial cases.
Schema equals truth
Validate output structure and separately evaluate grounding/correctness.
Blind retry loops
Retry only transient failures within a total deadline and record usage.
questions: What is prompt versioning?
Store template, examples, model/config and test results so comparisons are reproducible.
Why an adapter?
Provider SDK and transport details stay outside business logic and test contracts.
Can JSON mode guarantee a correct answer?
No; parseability, schema validity and factual correctness are different checks.

5.fast: C4 evaluation pipeline → handwritten cases/rubric → deterministic checks → small human calibration sample → judge experiment. Evaluate before agent complexity.
diagnostic: Working endpoint
Run the same request repeatedly and capture output/config.
Test separation
Distinguish HTTP correctness from answer usefulness.
Dataset hygiene
Keep development examples apart from release holdout.
pitfalls: One combined RAG score
Measure retrieval, citations, generation and system behavior separately.
Judge treated as ground truth
Compare human/judge disagreement and inspect bias and failure modes.
Threshold invented after results
State intended thresholds before comparing candidates; report sample counts and uncertainty.
questions: What belongs in a holdout?
Cases not used to tune prompts, retrieval settings or model selection.
Why calibrate an AI judge?
A judge can favor style, verbosity or a model family and miss real task failures.
What is an actionable eval failure?
A labeled failure tied to a reproducible case and an identifiable component or product requirement.
5.arabic_note: Arabic lifecycle material provides orientation. A complete Arabic course covering judge calibration, retrieval metrics and release-gate statistics was not verified; use C3/C4 and the English evaluation labs for those parts.

6.fast: F7 → Arabic mini-RAG PostgreSQL migration lesson → SQLAlchemy sessions/transactions → Alembic → ownership tests. Reuse your SQL knowledge.
diagnostic: SQL transfer
Use joins, foreign keys and transactions without a new beginner course.
API prerequisite
Pass IDs and caller identity through a typed application layer.
Persistence reasoning
Explain how Mongo document ownership maps to relational keys.
pitfalls: AsyncSession shared across requests
Use one session per request/task and explicit transaction boundaries.
Unscoped get-by-ID
Every user-owned query includes caller ownership or an authorized join.
Migration only works on your laptop
Test upgrade from empty DB and from the previous schema snapshot.
questions: Session versus transaction?
A session manages ORM state and work; a transaction defines the atomic database boundary.
Why migrations instead of create_all in production?
Changes must be versioned, reviewable and applied predictably to existing data.
What makes ingestion idempotent?
A stable identity/version key plus constraints and transaction logic prevent duplicate effects.

7.fast: G4/C6 retrieval basics → mini-RAG processing/search lessons → pgvector exact search → a labeled bilingual retrieval set. Keep page provenance before optimizing.
diagnostic: Database readiness
Persist owner/document/version/chunk metadata with tested ownership.
Vector readiness
Explain dot product and cosine and distinguish similarity from probability.
Corpus readiness
Use a small permitted textual corpus and list parsing limitations.
pitfalls: Text without provenance
Keep source ID, page, chunk ordinal, version and owner throughout ingestion.
Choosing an English-only embedding blindly
Test Arabic/English queries and follow model-card preprocessing.
ANN before a baseline
Use exact search to establish correctness and measure before adding an index.
questions: Why overlap chunks?
It can preserve boundary context but increases duplicates, cost and retrieval redundancy.
Why store an embedding model version?
Changing models or dimensions invalidates comparisons and may require re-indexing.
Can you filter after returning candidates?
Ownership must be enforced in retrieval; post-filtering alone can leak data or destroy recall.

8.fast: Measured exact retrieval → cited generation → no-evidence tests → hybrid/reranking experiments only for observed ranking failures.
diagnostic: L05 readiness
A labeled query set and separate component metrics exist.
L07 readiness
Each returned chunk has valid owner/source/page metadata.
Prompt readiness
A model adapter returns validated structured fields.
pitfalls: A citation string equals evidence
Resolve source IDs, inspect source content and assess support for the actual claim.
Hybrid search always improves
Use the same query set and compare recall/ranking/cost; retain a simpler baseline if better.
Reranking the entire corpus
Retrieve candidates first; rerank a bounded list and measure the latency increase.
questions: What does Recall@k tell you?
How much of the labeled relevant evidence appears among the first k results; define relevance granularity.
Why RRF?
It combines ranked lists without assuming their numeric scores are calibrated to each other.
What must abstention test?
No evidence, irrelevant evidence and conflicting evidence; the response should expose uncertainty rather than invent support.

9.fast: Read Anthropic before agent frameworks → inspect a context trace → budget and retrieve journals → add editable memory → test compaction only when needed.
diagnostic: RAG readiness
Explain which passages were retrieved and which reached the prompt.
State readiness
Conversations and journals are owner-scoped and deletable.
Evaluation readiness
Have multi-turn cases with expected facts and source evidence.
pitfalls: Append all history forever
Allocate a budget and retrieve only relevant state.
Summary treated as canonical truth
Link memories to sources and preserve correction/deletion behavior.
Multi-agent complexity for memory alone
Prove a single workflow fails before adding another agent.
questions: Prompt versus context engineering?
Prompt writing is part of choosing and managing all instructions, tools, evidence, history and state available to the model.
What is just-in-time retrieval?
Keep lightweight references and fetch detailed information only when the current step needs it.
When is compaction acceptable?
After measuring retained facts, lost constraints and future-task performance with recoverable source state.
9.arabic_note: Microsoft provides Arabic translated context/memory lessons. No complete Egyptian video course on context rot, compaction and memory evaluation was verified. The Anthropic article and English lessons are the primary sources for those techniques.

10.fast: F5 event-loop sections → a blocking-route experiment → F6 streaming → cancellation → mini-RAG Celery lessons and durable ingestion.
diagnostic: API readiness
Fake slow/error providers exist so tests are reproducible.
Persistence readiness
A job has stable IDs and persisted states.
Concurrency basics
Explain I/O waiting versus CPU work.
pitfalls: async around blocking code
A sync parser/model call still blocks; isolate it explicitly.
Retry duplicates writes
Use stable job identity and transactional effects.
Browser stops but provider continues
Propagate cancellation and record abandoned work and usage.
questions: When is BackgroundTasks insufficient?
When work must survive a process restart, needs retries/queues or long-running execution.
What does at-least-once imply?
The same task may execute more than once; effects must be idempotent.
Why bound concurrency?
To prevent pool exhaustion, provider rate-limit storms and unbounded memory usage.
10.arabic_note: The Arabic worker lessons cover Celery integration. Detailed Python cancellation, structured concurrency and disconnect semantics were not verified in a dedicated Arabic course; use Python/FastAPI docs and F5/F6 for those subtopics.

11.fast: Port your known auth concepts using F8 → test object ownership at every boundary → malicious-document fixtures → upload/rate/privacy controls.
diagnostic: Auth transfer
Explain JWT validation and role versus object permission.
RAG readiness
Document retrieval and source display are separate access paths.
Job readiness
Job IDs and state can be tied to a caller.
pitfalls: Prompt as an access-control system
Permission checks execute in backend code before data/tools are exposed.
Sanitize then trust everything
Treat retrieved text/tool output as untrusted throughout execution.
Log all prompts for debugging
Redact sensitive fields and define retention/erasure behavior.
questions: Authentication versus authorization?
Identity verification versus permission to perform a specific action on a specific object.
Why indirect prompt injection?
A document or tool result can carry instructions even when the user query is benign.
What is a safe reflection boundary?
Separate cited book content, personal journal facts and generated suggestions; avoid unsupported clinical claims.
11.arabic_note: Arabic translated security material introduces risks. No Arabic hands-on equivalent to the selected LLM security labs was verified; use the English labs for attack/defense practice.

12.fast: G5 tool concepts → Anthropic workflow patterns → one read-only tool → bounded loop → trajectory evaluation. Keep multi-agent work conditional.
diagnostic: RAG/security readiness
A caller-scoped search operation exists and rejects unauthorized access.
Contract readiness
Validate tool arguments and distinguish error from empty success.
Evaluation readiness
Measure task completion and tool behavior separately.
pitfalls: Every problem needs an agent
Compare with deterministic routing/workflows first.
Tool execution trusts model arguments
Validate schema and permission for every call, independent of model compliance.
Unbounded self-correction
Enforce steps, wall time and token/cost budgets in code.
questions: Workflow versus agent?
The workflow fixes control flow in code; the agent chooses next actions within enforced limits.
What is a trajectory failure?
An invalid/unnecessary/repeated tool sequence even if the final prose looks plausible.
When add sub-agents?
A separable task and a measured improvement justify coordination, isolation and extra cost.
12.arabic_note: Arabic translated agent lessons provide structured text. A complete Arabic course covering bounded loops plus trajectory evaluation was not verified; pair them with the English agent course and assessment labs.

13.fast: Official MCP architecture + Arabic translated index → Python SDK server/client → permission boundary → failure/reconnect tests. Use a single local integration first.
diagnostic: Tool prerequisites
A typed read-only operation already works without MCP.
Security prerequisites
Caller identity and tool/data permissions are explicit.
Protocol reasoning
Distinguish app orchestration, transport and model behavior.
pitfalls: MCP grants permission automatically
Protocol interoperability is separate from authorization.
SDK example without version pin
Pin SDK/protocol and document transport compatibility.
Remote server output becomes trusted instructions
Validate and scope results; keep business decisions in application code.
questions: Host/client/server?
The host application manages model interaction, the client maintains a server connection, and the server exposes capabilities.
Tools versus resources?
Tools perform callable operations; resources expose addressable context. Neither bypasses permissions.
Why not add MCP everywhere?
Use it for interoperable external integrations; direct internal calls can be simpler.
13.arabic_note: The verified Arabic MCP resource is a translated curriculum with code links. No comparable Egyptian video course was verified; use the Anthropic course plus official SDK examples for implementation.

14.fast: F12 selective Docker → mini-RAG deployment lessons → CI + immutable version metadata → trace one request → backup/restore and rollback drill.
diagnostic: Application readiness
API, database and worker run locally with known setup commands.
Test readiness
Fast deterministic suite and bounded eval cases run independently.
Ops reasoning
Distinguish liveness, readiness, migration and dependency failure.
pitfalls: Container runs therefore production-ready
Test persistence, health, secrets, worker restart and restore.
Only log final model text
Trace parser/retriever/provider stages while redacting private content.
Deploy with no recovery plan
Test restore/rollback and define who can apply a migration.
questions: What belongs in a trace?
A correlation ID, stage timing, selected model/config and safe error/usage attributes; avoid raw private journals.
What must be versioned?
Code, model, prompt, corpus/index, embedding/chunk policy and evaluation set.
Backup equals restore?
No; a backup is evidence only after a successful restore and consistency check.

15.fast: C4 model selection → comparable runs → C9 metrics → one bottleneck experiment → C10 feedback loop. Keep quality gates active during optimization.
diagnostic: Baseline readiness
Quality, citation, security and latency results have version metadata.
Observability readiness
Measure stage timing and usage without private content logging.
Selection discipline
Hold corpus/prompt/eval fixed for model comparison.
pitfalls: Leaderboard wins equal product wins
Evaluate your bilingual corpus and workload under actual constraints.
Global cache key
Include ownership, model/prompt/corpus versions and deletion invalidation.
Thumbs-up equals ground truth
Feedback is biased and sparse; review failure examples before changing behavior.
questions: Why p95 as well as p50?
Median hides slow tail experiences; report concurrency and sample count too.
Cost per request?
Measure input/output tokens and provider prices or local compute assumptions, plus retries/reranking when relevant.
When optimize?
After a reproducible bottleneck is identified and a quality/permission regression gate exists.
15.arabic_note: Arabic lifecycle and deployment material provides context. Dedicated Arabic instruction for controlled model selection, tail latency and cache isolation was not verified; use C4/C9/C10 and the English engineering material.

16.fast: No new large course: assemble the evidence, run an untouched holdout, ship a reproducible release and defend the decisions. Apply while improving documented gaps.
diagnostic: Core project readiness
Upload, ask, cite, journal connection, history and deletion work end-to-end.
Evidence readiness
CI, holdout, security matrix and traces have reproducible artifacts.
Independence
Modify and test a small feature without generated code.
pitfalls: Another demo without evidence
Link reproducible tests, datasets, configs and failure analysis.
Production claim exceeds deployment
Describe what was exercised and remaining limits precisely.
Study every optional resource before applying
Use the role checklist and apply after demonstrable core competence.
questions: How defend a rejected technology?
State the requirement, options, evidence, tradeoff and trigger for reconsidering the decision.
What makes a CV metric credible?
A reproducible measurement with workload, sample size, environment and configuration.
How present failure?
Show the case, root cause, mitigation, verification and remaining limitation.
16.arabic_note: Arabic project orientation and UX/lifecycle lessons support presentation. A verified Arabic AI-engineering interview bank was not found. The Level self-checks and mock defense are recommendations, not official ITI interview questions.

17.fast: Optional: C7 go/no-go → curated train/dev/holdout data → one small LoRA experiment → compare to baseline → serve only if justified.
diagnostic: Failure evidence
Show a task failure that prompting, retrieval or model choice did not solve.
Training readiness
Explain loss, optimizer, leakage and held-out evaluation.
Budget readiness
Choose hardware/runtime and stop conditions before any training run.
pitfalls: Fine-tuning for changing factual documents
RAG may be a better mechanism; demonstrate the actual adaptation need.
Train/eval near-duplicates
Split by source or task group and audit leakage.
Quantization improves everything
Measure memory, speed and quality; hardware compatibility varies.
questions: When fine-tune?
When a stable task/behavior gap and sufficient representative data justify training and maintenance costs.
What is LoRA?
A parameter-efficient adaptation method using trainable low-rank updates instead of full-weight training.
What must compare?
The same independent task cases before/after tuning, including regressions, memory, latency and cost.
17.arabic_note: Arabic translated fine-tuning material supplies concepts. No complete Arabic course on the specific PEFT/SFT/versioned-serving workflow was verified; current Hugging Face/vLLM resources are primary for the experiment.

18.fast: Optional supporting UI: Elzero TypeScript gaps → React official quick path → fetch/abort → source display and browser tests. A minimal client is sufficient.
diagnostic: JavaScript transfer
Use promises, modules and HTTP requests without a full JS course.
Backend readiness
Stable auth, upload, question and source endpoints exist.
Product contract
Define streaming events and the citation response schema.
pitfalls: Full frontend specialization
Implement only the capstone user flows.
Client guards replace backend auth
Server ownership tests remain mandatory.
Render model output as arbitrary HTML
Use safe rendering and explicit source links; avoid unsanitized HTML.
questions: Why a discriminated union for API results?
It forces success/error/stream states to be handled explicitly.
Why AbortController?
It cancels a fetch/stream and lets the UI stop unnecessary work.
What proves usable citations?
Keyboard-accessible source links resolve to authorized passages with page/context and clear loading/error states.
18.arabic_note: Elzero provides Arabic TypeScript teaching. This Level uses English React/MDN docs for current React, stream consumption and accessibility; a React-specific Arabic playlist was not verified in this pass.
